question.text: Under SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/OIAE/OIAE_IAD-1/P/CIR/2023/131 dated July 31, 2023, AIFs are required to:

answer.text: Maintain a physical ombudsman office in every SEBI regional center
Refuse all disputes that cannot be resolved within 7 days

Enrol on the MII-established ODR (Online Dispute Resolution) Portal, display a link to the ODR Portal on the home page of their websites and mobile apps, and ensure implementation of related processes
Charge a dispute-resolution fee from the complainant

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the AIF Managers workbook on SCORES and Online Dispute Resolution (pp. 307-309), AIFs must enrol on the ODR Portal established by Market Infrastructure Institutions, ensure implementation of related processes, execute electronic agreements with the MIIs and ODR institutions, display the link to the ODR Portal on the home page of their website and mobile application, and train staff on the SCORES and ODR processes. The 21-day SCORES timeline for grievance redressal is also covered on pp. 307-308. The Trap: A physical ombudsman office in every SEBI regional centre is not required by the source. Refusing all disputes that cannot be resolved within 7 days contradicts the 21-day SCORES timeline. Charging the complainant a dispute-resolution fee is not part of the source's prescribed ODR architecture. Note: The mandatory enrolment, the link on the home page of the website and mobile application, the electronic agreements with the MIIs/ODR institutions, and the staff training described on pp. 307-309 together form the ODR compliance package for AIFs.
